CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

jlbind is an R package that lets other R packages (“clients”) call Julia code compiled ahead of time with juliac --trim=safe, with no Julia session at run time. An R process can host only one compiled Julia image, so jlbind compiles the binding packages of every installed client into one shared library that all of them bind to. vignettes/jlbind.qmd (installing and using clients) and vignettes/writing-clients.qmd (writing a client) are the user-facing guides (rendered with Quarto); keep them in sync with user-visible behavior. vignettes/articles/performance.qmd is a pkgdown-only article whose data comes from vignettes/articles/performance/benchmark.R.

Commands

devtools::document() # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen
devtools::test() # unit tests (no Julia needed)
devtools::test(filter = "entrypoints") # one test file (test-entrypoints.R)
devtools::check() # R CMD check

Git hooks are managed with prek from .pre-commit-config.yaml: panache (Markdown), air (R formatting), jarl (R lint) and a roxygen-up-to-date check. Run them with prek run --all-files. Tests run in the package namespace, so call internal functions directly rather than via jlbind::: (jarl flags it).

The integration test (tests/testthat/test-integration.R) installs the two clients in tests/clients/ into a temp library, compiles them into one library and calls them from a fresh R process. It takes a minute or more and only runs with Julia >= 1.13 and JLBIND_TEST_BUILD=true:

JLBIND_TEST_BUILD=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "integration")'

A second integration test builds a copy of hellojl with Config/jlbind/trim: false (an untrimmed, ~200 MB library); it runs only with JLBIND_TEST_NOTRIM=true.

Environment variables: JULIA (Julia binary to use), JLBIND_LIBRARY (load this library instead of the one install_backend() builds, or the one build_library() writes to a load_all()ed client’s .jlbind/), JULIA_NUM_THREADS.

CI (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) runs R CMD check with Julia 1.13 on Linux/Windows/macOS and with the latest Julia 1.x on Linux, all with the integration test enabled, and once on Linux without Julia, which is what CRAN sees — everything except the integration test must pass without Julia. test-coverage.yaml runs covr with Julia 1.13 and JLBIND_TEST_BUILD=true and uploads to Codecov; pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site.

Architecture

Three layers, spread across R, Julia and C:

  • inst/julia/JLBind/ — Julia package that clients’ binding packages depend on: R C API via ccall (rapi.jl), from_sexp/to_sexp conversions (convert.jl), RRef{T} external-pointer registry (refs.jl), and the @rcall macro (rcall.jl) that exports <Module>_<f> as a @ccallable, returning errors as a jlbind_error character vector rather than unwinding. set_threads.c is compiled into the library and called via .C. JLBind is not registered: builds Pkg.develop the copy shipped in the installed R package.
  • inst/julia/build.jl — the compile step, invoked by the R side. It copies everything to writable scratch dirs, generates a JLBindImage package importing JLBind and every binding package, seeds dependencies from the first client’s Manifest.toml (falling back to [compat] resolution), and compiles with JuliaC in a separate environment.
  • R side (R/) — backend.R: install_backend() / build_library() (finds clients, runs build.jl, stores the library under R_user_dir("jlbind", "data")/backend/ with the client versions it was built from). clients.R: client discovery via the Config/jlbind DESCRIPTION field. runtime.R: bind(pkg) called from a client’s .onLoad, loads the library once, sets threads, binds a client only if the library was built from its installed version. scaffold.R: use_jlbind() and update_entrypoints(), which scans @rcall declarations (with comments/strings blanked, so they must be literal top-level @rcalls) and writes src/entrypoints.h. julia.R: locating Julia.

Each client carries a generated C shim: src/jlbind.c (from inst/templates/init.c) plus src/entrypoints.h (an X-macro list of JLBIND_ENTRY(name, nargs, params, args)). The shim registers each routine itself and forwards to the combined library through function pointers resolved when jlbind calls the client’s jlbind_bind routine.

The test clients in tests/clients/{hellojl,counterjl} are scaffolded output: their src/jlbind.c, src/entrypoints.h and R/jlbind.R correspond to inst/templates/ and update_entrypoints(). When changing a template or the header generator, update the test clients to match.

Constraints to keep in mind

  • Everything in the library is compiled with --trim=safe, so every Julia call must be statically resolvable. A function receiving an abstract RRef{T} must take it as @nospecialize(x::T) and branch on concrete types; Core.invoke is not accepted by trim verification (Julia 1.13).
  • @R(sym) must name R.dll on Windows; Windows builds record julia_bindir so R can find the Julia runtime before loading the DLL.
  • Never write into an installed package directory; builds work on scratch copies.
  • experiments/two-libs/ (excluded from the build) demonstrates why two juliac libraries cannot coexist in one process.
